_what_this_is: The machine-checked statement of every load-bearing registered rule, one entry each, and the single place each value is written. docs/preregistration.md prose must reference these rather than restate them: the defect this file exists to stop is a rule stated in several places across several amendments, where a session reads the earliest and takes it for current. On 15 October 2026 the floor rule alone appeared on 44 lines of the registration, 16 of them normative, across four revisions.
_how_it_is_enforced: tests/test_registration_matches_the_code.py asserts every entry against the implementation named in code_location. A rule changed in code without changing this file fails the suite; a rule changed here without changing the code fails too. That is the half of the problem an amendment list cannot catch, because a code change that nobody wrote an amendment for leaves no trace in the document at all.
_amending: Change the value here in the same commit as the code, and mark the commit with an Amends: <rule_id> trailer so docs/amendment_history.md can be generated from the log rather than hand-maintained. The generated history is committed, because a rebase that squashes or drops a commit would otherwise lose a registration record silently.

floor_rule.means: No magnitude floor. The decision rests on the paired interval on model minus best baseline; effect sizes are reported in standard errors of the available precision. Registered 15 October 2026 (the owner: "no floor. paired interval").

alpha_one_sided.means: The tested model is a candidate at one-sided 0.05: H1 first, then its second-stage family by Holm at the same level, so the smaller of H2 and P1 faces 0.025 and the larger faces 0.05. Holm over eight hypotheses was withdrawn on 8 October 2026. The level was halved to 0.025 while two models were tested, where the union bound over two uncorrected tests put the familywise chance of a lucky pass at 2 x 0.025 = 0.05. With tested_models holding one model from 22 October 2026 there is no across-model multiplicity left, the familywise level is this level itself, and the halving no longer buys anything, so it was returned to 0.05 (the owner, 22 October 2026: "Move it back to the .05 alpha please with just one model now"; decision 9.78). This is the more permissive of the two readings of the same registered familywise 0.05 and it was taken before any lockbox was drawn.
superseded: 0.025, one-sided, per model while two models were tested

tested_models.means: One model: the noisy-OR configuration of the linear-response encoder. The sigmoid head was dropped on 15 October 2026 because only noisy-OR has modules that can be read as pathways; the message-passing encoder moved to robustness_models on 22 October 2026 (the owner: "Defer it to robustness. I don't want it constraining things because this is more about mechanistically identifiably predictive nosology"). The registered reason is that only the linear-response encoder has a closed-form steady state, so only there can the sensitivity of a label to a sign-disputed edge, and hence whether a disputed sign is identifiable at all, be read without a training run. With one tested model the familywise chance of a lucky pass is the level the model is tested at, which is why alpha_one_sided returned to 0.05 in the same session (decision 9.78): the registered familywise 0.05 is unchanged and is now carried by one test rather than split across two.
superseded: confirmatory_v2_message_passing_noisy_or and confirmatory_v2_linear_response_noisy_or, each at one-sided 0.025

robustness_models.means: Read and reported with their intervals outside the tested family, spending no alpha, as the two permutation readings have since 8 October 2026. The message-passing encoder sits here from 22 October 2026 so a conclusion of the tested model can be checked against a second encoder of a different inductive bias without that check constraining the registered family. A robustness reading that disagrees is reported as a disagreement and cannot withdraw the tested model's result; the corroboration a second tested model would have given is therefore given up, which is the cost the owner accepted.
robustness_models.code_location: configs/head_choice.json robustness values, scored by experiments/score_confirmatory.py --models

held_out_fraction.means: One seventh of each side: the genes by the registered disease-cluster grouping and the drugs by the item 25 target rule. A convention fixed before the split rule existed, not derived.

bootstrap_unit.means: A cluster bootstrap over leakage groups rather than perturbations, so the dependence among perturbations sharing disease annotations or targets stays inside a resample.

num_bootstrap.means: Resamples in the deciding paired bootstrap, the same rows for every model, seed and baseline.

minimum_positives_to_score.means: A symptom enters the macro average with at least five positives and one negative among the labelled rows.

normalisation.means: Each edge is divided by the destination's in-degree summed over every relation, counting only the edges whose source the seed can reach, per seed; unsigned row sums over the edges that carry are one. Amendment item 28 as narrowed by decision 9.16.

validation_fold_rule.means: The early-stopping validation fold rotates with the seed over round(1 / 0.15) = 7 grouped folds, so seeds 0 to 4 use folds 0 to 4 and folds 5 and 6 never serve as validation. The registration said "fold 0" until 15 October 2026, which described seed 0 alone.

label_likelihood.means: Every pair the label selection keeps is counted once, at its code length under a positive-unlabelled likelihood (models/positive_unlabelled_likelihood.py): a labelled positive -log(b + (1 - b) pi f), an unlabelled pair -log(1 - b) - log(1 - pi f) and an evidenced negative -log(1 - a f), f the probability that the link is real. The labelling propensity pi at the median literature popularity is w + (1 - w) r(t, s) per perturbation type and symptom, w the registered negative weight 0.2 and r(t, s) the cell's labelled share on the fit rows, which keeps every cell's registered constant optimum and is above every share; one popularity slope is learned when a literature table is named. The false-report rate b is 0; the power a of a never-above-placebo negative is amendment item 3's n_effective / (n_effective + 214.39), 0.5 where the label states no arm sizes. Replaces the weighted cross-entropy of amendment item 3 (a silent pair at 0.2, an evidenced negative at its placebo weight, a positive at its evidence weight); decision 9.90.
superseded: weighted: a positive at its evidence weight, an unlabelled pair at 0.2, a never-above-placebo negative at 0.5 or n_effective / (n_effective + 214.39) (amendment item 3)
